subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does the gateway security owner confirm that the reported event sequence number is outside the authentication/session boundary and that this public issue can close without a code change?
rationale: Source inspection strongly contradicts the claimed exploit, but the protected `security` label requires explicit human security-owner disposition before closure.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Confirm that event sequence numbers are ordering-only metadata, close the public issue, and request a private advisory only if the reporter has a working boundary-bypass proof.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open temporarily while asking the reporter to privately provide a packet trace or proof showing unauthorized dispatch after authentication checks.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that event sequence numbers are ordering-only metadata, close the public issue, and request a private advisory only if the reporter has a working boundary-bypass proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work directly owns gateway authentication, pairing, scope clamping, and device authorization on this path.
